parts.text: A student investigates the effect of insulation on the cooling of water. She uses the apparatus shown in Fig. 1.1. The sides of beaker A are covered with material that is a thermal insulator. Beaker B has no covering on its sides. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Record room temperature θ R shown on the thermometer in Fig. 1.1. θ R = .......................................................... [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student pours 150 cm 3 of hot water into beaker A and records the temperature θ at time t = 0. She records, in Table 1.1, the temperature of the water in the beaker every 30 s. The student repeats the process for beaker B. Add units to the column headings in Table 1.1. [1] Table 1.1 beaker A with insulation beaker B without insulation t / θ / θ / 0 88.0 87.5 30 86.0 83.5 60 84.5 81.5 90 83.5 80.0 120 82.5 79.0 150 82.0 78.5 180 81.5 78.0

parts.label: i
parts.text: (e) (i) Calculate the average cooling rate x 1 during the first half of the experiment for the water in beaker B. Use the readings for beaker B from Table 1.1 and the equation x 1 = θ 0 – θ 90 T , where T = 90 s and θ 0 and θ 90 are the temperatures of the water in beaker B at t = 0 and t = 90 s. Include the unit. x 1 = .......................................................... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the average cooling rate x 2 during the second half of the experiment for the water in beaker B. Use the readings for beaker B from Table 1.1 and the equation x 2 = θ 90 – θ 180 T , where T = 90 s and θ 90 and θ 180 are the temperatures of the water in beaker B at t = 90 s and t = 180 s. Include the unit. x 2 = .......................................................... [1]
